newsitem.title: JAPAN: Japan firm says Russia oil investment difficult.
newsitem.headline: Japan firm says Russia oil investment difficult.

text.p: Major infrastructural, tax and policy improvements need to be made before Russia's rich energy resources can be fully tapped, a Japanese exploration firm official said on Tuesday.

"From experience in taking part in Russian energy projects, I can say the environment is still tough and that many difficult problems exist," said Takeshi Kaneko, managing director of Itochu Oil Exploration Co Ltd, a subsidiary of major trading house Itochu Corp.

Kaneko told a seminar on investing in Russia's energy sector that a possible devaluation of the rouble was a constant worry, because under Russian accounting principles, budgets have to be denominated in roubles not dollars.
Frequent changes to the taxation and exportation systems have also caused headaches, he said.

And contracts for pipeline transportation, which is dominated by one firm, are renewed on an annual basis. Oil development, however, requires a long-term prospective and therefore long-term contracts, he said.
Another cause for concern is a growing movement within Russia to review joint-venture export rights, he said.
The revisions may restrict about 60 to 70 percent of a joint venture's oil sales to within Russia, and expose venture members to risks due to lower prices and payments, he said.
Kaneko also said a lack of information on Russian companies was a problem for foreign companies which are interested in acquiring part or all of a Russian firm.

Itochu Oil Exploration Co Ltd is currently involved in joint ventures which develop, produce, transport, export and sell supplies from an oil field in western Siberia and the Volga oil field in the Urals.
The company is also a partner in the Sakhalin 1 project through the Sakhalin Oil and Gas Development Co Ltd joint venture.
